summary: In this excerpt from Book 2, the narrator escapes a motel with Courtney Polk after a dirty police officer tries to take her. He hotwires a black GMC truck, zigzags through the desert outskirts, and switches cars to avoid pursuit. He asks Courtney about Pithica, which she has never heard of, then calls a contact named Rio, who warns him not to get involved.
one_line: The narrator flees a crooked cop with Courtney Polk, questions her about 'Pithica,' and is warned off by Rio.
key_facts: The narrator hotwires a black GMC truck, caked with dust so it looked gray, and gets the engine running in fourteen seconds.
The narrator suspects the police officer was dirty and hoped to find his car, badge and ID for leverage, but no promising vehicle was visible.
Courtney Polk had been a drug mule and was locked in a basement by the cartel.
The narrator asks Courtney Polk whether she was after the cop's target, and she replies that she has never heard of Pithica.
The narrator wonders why a peace officer was on the take after Courtney Polk.
The narrator avoids going straight into LA, zigzagging through the brown desert of the northern outskirts and switching cars twice in three hours.
Once the morning hit a decent hour, the narrator buys a disposable cell phone at a cheap electronics store.
The narrator calls Rio and says 'Pithica'; Rio responds, 'Don't get involved.'
The narrator replies, 'I'm already involved,' and Rio says he can't talk.
